question: Why was the post-Maurya era also known as the era of reorganisation?
options: Because the end of centralized Mauryan rule led not to decay, but to the reorganization of powerful regional kingdoms ac
explanation: Because the end of centralized Mauryan rule led not to decay, but to the reorganization of powerful regional kingdoms across India. These kingdoms established flourishing trade networks, minted distinct coins, fostered art and literature, and assimilated foreign influxes into Indian culture.

question: How did foreign ruling groups like the Indo-Greeks, Shakas, and Kushanas assimilate into Indian society?
options: 1. Religious Adoption: Foreign rulers embraced Indian faiths—Heliodorus (Indo-Greek) erected a Garuda pillar to Vishnu;
explanation: 1. Religious Adoption: Foreign rulers embraced Indian faiths—Heliodorus (Indo-Greek) erected a Garuda pillar to Vishnu; Kanishka (Kushana) patronized Buddhism. 2. Coinage & Language: They issued coins with Brahmi/Kharosthi legends alongside Greek, portraying Indian deities (Shiva, Buddha). 3. Artistic Synthesis: Fused Hellenistic realistic art styles with Indian iconography, developing Gandhara art. 4. Cultural Confluence: Adopted Indian names, royal customs, and married into local families, becoming integral to Indian society.
